According to the Lyon hypothesis, all but one X chromosome in each cell is inactivated and forms a Barr body. Therefore, with three X chromosomes, two will be inactivated, resulting in two Barr bodies. The retrieved evidence paths do not directly relate to the formation of Barr bodies and are not relevant to this specific question. Thus, the correct answer is that a man with a karyotype of 48, XXXY will have two Barr corpuscles.
analysis: Barr bodies are inactivated X chromosomes found in the cells of individuals with more than one X chromosome. In a typical female (46, XX), there is one Barr body. In a male with karyotype 48, XXXY, there are three X chromosomes. The number of Barr bodies is calculated as the total number of X chromosomes minus one. Therefore, a 48, XXXY individual would have two Barr bodies.
